monitor. But that's the problem. Lots of people never calibrate their
monitors, and so their light colors are all blown out. You might send
people to a web site like this: http://www.photofriday.com/calibrate.php
if they can't see the light grey.

-Harlan

messages.author: 66a7bbbceef834e9
messages.subject: Re: Greys
parts:
Hi all, I've done an faceted graphic of multiple variables. And the
order of the bars changes between the treatments (ie: RA $ RD) and the
facets.

Here is the code:
p3<- ggplot(datos_medias, aes(x=t_forestal, y=V1,
fill=interaction(t_edad,t_humedad)))
p3<-p3+geom_bar(position='dodge', stat='identity')
p3<-p3+facet_wrap(~variable, scales='free')
etiquetas<- paste(rep(c(1,5),3),rep(c('Control','Húmedo','Seco'),each=2))
p3<-p3+scale_fill_brewer('Edad*Humedad',
labels=etiquetas)+scale_x_discrete('Tratamiento
Forestal')+scale_y_continuous('Media')

And attached is the result.
How can I make the order the same for the treatments and the facets?
Luciano

messages.author: 599a13812d4cd3e8
messages.subject: Re: Greys
parts:
I wonder whether trying to get it right for all circumstances is the
best approach; projectors and screens vary so much. I wonder if it
might be possible to have a "test pattern" which one could throw up on
one's 'best guess' projector/printer and then choose the limit value
that way. ie. have a function that prints out a test PDF, then read
off a code from that, then feed that code to set_theme() for actually
producing graphs.

Of course in some situations you're just dealing with such terrible
contrast that knowing ahead of time that you're limited to four of
five gradients that can be reliably distinguished; that sucks but
knowing it ahead of time is better than finding out during your
presentation.

--J

On Tue, Nov 24, 2009 at 23:05, James Howison
<ja...@freelancepropaganda.com> wrote:
> I wonder whether trying to get it right for all circumstances is the
> best approach; projectors and screens vary so much.

Just to confirm this: with the default settings of our projector
(newish sony, I can get the exact model if you want) everything is
white after 85-86. It has a cut-to-white function which some jerk
apparently thought was such good idea to improve contrast that it is
set by default. With the proper settings, I can clearly make out the
current background colour (grey90 if I read the code right) from
white. And of course the projector won't retain my settings. So in
addition to variability in projectors, projectors settings also vary
and to a much wider extent than (LCD) screens. I would solve the
problem of projectors by advising to use theme_bw() when in doubt.

JiHO
